### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6f4c518b012a3959ba6c7d414b5fa085ad135c17` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fadfc9acc8ec12a7ecaaa8b55feac525596b8df0` — the merge of head `38728b3e1b37ed00bed9da54be08198fd7fe1bd8` into base `6f4c518b012a3959ba6c7d414b5fa085ad135c17`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fadfc9acc8ec12a7ecaaa8b55feac525596b8df0 && git checkout fadfc9acc8ec12a7ecaaa8b55feac525596b8df0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6f4c518b012a3959ba6c7d414b5fa085ad135c17 38728b3e1b37ed00bed9da54be08198fd7fe1bd8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6f4c518b012a3959ba6c7d414b5fa085ad135c17 && git merge --no-ff 38728b3e1b37ed00bed9da54be08198fd7fe1bd8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6f4c518b012a3959ba6c7d414b5fa085ad135c17
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6f4c518b012a3959ba6c7d414b5fa085ad135c17` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `56d63b4e79e18dbb7311d97dda88ab2c54b906e0`
Local-runs: probe — `npm pack @objectstack/spec@18.0.0-next.0` into a new empty scratch directory, read with `grep`/`sed` only (its integrity matches the packument), to verify the release claims the changeset and the DELIBERATE CORRECTION rest on: tarball `CHANGELOG.md:2091` and `:2093`, and that the published next.0 refuses every table row and the sub-day members with the text this PR replaces.

**Verdict in one paragraph.** Everything this head's own diff changes is right: the seven strings and the interval refusal name the release that actually stops accepting each shape, the pin derives that release correctly in both directions under the prerelease label, the changeset is true sentence by sentence at `patch` / `Clause-②: no`, the `RETIRED_SUB_DAY_INTERVALS` TSDoc is true, and the DELIBERATE CORRECTION on `.changeset/pre/22876` is CONFIRMED. The FAIL is about the tree this head will land on, not the diff: `origin/main` moved after the dev's last sweep (merge base `d889448b9`), and it now carries two more `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` conversions (`page-action-row-navigation-executor-to-url`, `cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted`; 7 such entries, the PR's enumeration counts 5) and one new prescription of exactly this card's class, `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:193` "`view.data.provider: 'api'` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17", for a shape that is live at the 17.7.0 tag (`view.zod.ts:190`, `provider: z.literal('api')`, commit `1912af47b` landed 2026-10-13T08:47Z, after next.0 published). On the merged tree the pin's completeness guard ("every entry retired after the newest published stable release is joined") refuses the two unjoined ids, and `ci.yml` runs `Test Core` on `merge_group`, so this head cannot land green through the queue; and the card's nail ("fix all of them in one PR") is no longer met on `main`. The remedy is one round: merge `origin/main`; join the two new ids to `JOIN` with the prescriptions their surfaces render and correct any that name 17; correct `view.zod.ts:193` (and any literal pin on it) to 18; re-count the enumeration; re-request the at-tier review on the new head. Everything below carries over to that head unchanged.

**Inputs read.** Card #23145 body and all 10 comments; PR #23186 body in full, its 4 comments, its 21-file list and the net diff against `main`; the 50 check-runs on the head; `origin/main` at `01a3421f4`/`197fbe2c0` and the head tree read-only (the shared checkout's `FETCH_HEAD` was moved by another fetch mid-review, so every head read was re-pinned to the 40-hex sha, and one early merge-base reading taken off the moved ref was discarded); the 17.7.0 tag tree `4e4e88142`, which is on `origin/main`'s history (the clone is shallow below it, so 17.4.0 and 17.5.0 trees are not readable here); the npm packument (`latest` 17.7.0, `next` 18.0.0-next.0 published 2026-10-13T08:35:43Z, no 17.8.0 exists, nothing published between 17.7.0 and next.0). `/home/user/objectstack` has no `node_modules`, so the three `@changesets/*` citations were read from the lockfile-pinned copies (`pnpm-lock.yaml` on `origin/main` pins `read@1.0.1`, `assemble-release-plan@7.0.0`, `apply-release-plan@8.1.1`) in a sibling worktree's pnpm store.

**Check-runs on the head.** First read (about 10:55Z): 50 runs — 28 success, 10 skipped, 3 failure (all `Check Changeset`, the by-design red below), 9 `in_progress`. Second read (about 11:10Z, after the coordinator's notice): 51 runs — 35 success, 10 skipped, 4 failure, 2 `in_progress` (`Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`). The fourth failure is `Test Core (1/6)`, job 115256817478, completed 2026-10-13T11:06:01Z: by the seat's reading of its log (card comment 6144192235), the PR's own pin fails its completeness guard at `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts:248` on the two unjoined `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` entries named in the verdict paragraph — which is exactly what the merged-tree reading below predicts, so I take it as read. `Build Core`, `Test Core` 2/5/6, all four `Type Check` lanes (source gates included), every Lint lane, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green. The contract is judged on the diff; the red is judged in ① and in the verdict.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set: unchanged — verified, not only claimed.** The diff edits string literals and one TSDoc sentence: `elementFlatBindingRetired`'s shared template and the `defaultFilters` guidance (`ui/component.zod.ts`), `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_CATEGORY_REMOVED` / `EMAIL_TEMPLATE_IS_SYSTEM_REMOVED`, `PLUGIN_PERMISSIONS_LIST_FORM`, `STORAGE_SCOPE_PUBLIC_RETIRED`, the `allowOrgOverride` guidance, `timeUpdateIntervalRefusalMessage`. No `retiredKey(`, `enumWithRetiredValues(`, enum, union or `.strict()` construct moves; the file list touches neither `conversions/registry.ts` nor `migrations/**`; `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays `18.0.0`. Nothing is accepted or refused differently. RIGHT.

**Public surface that does change, each named right:**
- Shipped refusal text, 7 strings rendering 17 prescriptions. All 16 table rows are LIVE at the 17.7.0 tag tree (`4e4e88142`: `defaultFilters` as `z.array(…)` at `component.zod.ts:4498`; the ten element keys at `:2585/:2606`, `:2995/:3041/:3054/:3064`, `:4075/:4093/:4095/:4097`; `category`/`isSystem` at `email-template.zod.ts:106/:193`; the string-list arm at `manifest.zod.ts:94-95`; `'public'` at `object-storage.zod.ts:40`; `allowOrgOverride: z.boolean()` at `metadata-plugin.zod.ts:267`) and REFUSED in the published 18.0.0-next.0 (probe: `dist` carries the old text for every row — 56 hits of `removed in @objectstack/spec 17 (ADR-0087 D2)`, 16 each of the two `email_template` strings, 20 of the manifest list string, 6 of `17.8.0`, 18 of the release-less `allowOrgOverride` string, 0 of `removed in @objectstack/spec 18`; the `[REMOVED]` describes sit in `json-schema/ui/ObjectGridProps.json`, `json-schema/system/EmailTemplateDefinition.json`, `json-schema/ui/ElementRepeaterProps.json`, `json-schema/kernel/MetadataTypeRegistryEntry.json`). No release lies between 17.7.0 and 18.0.0-next.0. So "removed in @objectstack/spec 18" / "renamed … in @objectstack/spec 18" names the release that stops accepting each shape. RIGHT, all 16 rows.
- The sub-day `TimeUpdateInterval` refusal, "retired in protocol 18" to "removed in @objectstack/spec 17.5.0": the retirement (#17296, `9c44eed`) is an entry of the `## 17.5.0` section of `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` (line 18689 under the header at 7980); the committed census's 17.4.0 row (73 ids) does not carry `cube-sub-day-granularities-removed`; the registry stamps it `retiredAfter: '17.4.0'`; the refusal is already present at the 17.7.0 tag (`analytics.zod.ts:164-169`). 17.4.0 accepts, 17.5.0 refuses. RIGHT.
- JSON Schema `[REMOVED]` descriptions: `retiredKey()` describes as `[REMOVED] ${guidance}` (`retired-key.ts:186`), so the 14 key tombstones' describes carry the corrected text; the three regenerated `content/docs/references/**` pages (1 + 2 + 11 = 14 rows) follow byte-for-byte. RIGHT.
- `.d.ts` text: the `RETIRED_SUB_DAY_INTERVALS` TSDoc now reads "declared through @objectstack/spec 17.4.0; 17.5.0 removed them" — TRUE by the three readings above. The `(#17296)` citation was already there, resolves per the dev's diff-scoped `check-issue-citations` run, and `check:doc-authoring` governs runtime strings, not comments.
- Every `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence is untouched and right: `--from N` replays the majors above N, so `--from 17` replays the step-18 chain (the next.0 notes say the same at `CHANGELOG.md:468`).

**The 219 unchanged rows, sampled adversarially — on the head.** `packages/spec/src/**` (non-test) at the head has 0 hits for `17.8.0`, 0 for `retired in protocol 18`, exactly 7 for `@objectstack/spec 18` (the seven edited strings) and 202 for `removed in @objectstack/spec 17`. The discriminator for this class is whether a tombstone landed after the 17.7.0 cut. `git diff` from the `main` commit at the 17.7.0 publish time (`1c563af40`, 2026-10-06T12:06Z) to the head, spec sources non-test, adds exactly these `retiredKey(` / `enumWithRetiredValues(` lines: `allowOrgOverride`, `category`, `isSystem`, `StorageScopeSchema`, the ten element keys, `defaultFilters` — the rows this PR edits and nothing else; the only added lines naming a 17 release are the new `17.5.0` interval line and a relocated `'pdf'` `exportOptions` refusal that already existed at the tag (`view.zod.ts:2351-2364`), so it is 17.x-shipped and outside this class. The three controls (`breadcrumb` 17.5.0, `defaultSort` 17.2.0, `quickAdd` 17.4.0) keep "17" and are pin-joined; the fifth `17.7.0` entry at the merge base, `declared-index-unique-scope`, says "retired at protocol 18" (major 18) and is pin-joined. On the head, no string the diff leaves alone names a wrong release for a shape of this class.

**The same sample on `origin/main` — WRONG, and the reason for the verdict.** Since the merge base, `main` added `view.zod.ts:193` "`view.data.provider: 'api'` was removed in @objectstack/spec 17 (ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove)" (`1912af47b`, "retire the view-level `api` data source", 2026-10-13T08:47Z). The shape is live at the 17.7.0 tag (`view.zod.ts:190`) and no 17.x release after 17.7.0 exists, so the string must name 18; it is a D3-only retirement (`migrations/entries/semantic/18.view-data-api-provider-retired.ts`), so the derived pin cannot reach it. `main` also added two D2 conversions stamped `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` (`page-action-row-navigation-executor-to-url`, `cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted`, both `toMajor: 18`), which the pin's completeness guard requires joined and which `JOIN` does not name — a RED on the merged tree, not a passing one.

**The pin (`shared/retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts`).**
- Derivation: `removalMajor(retiredAfter)` gives `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` when `retiredAfter` is at or above the newest recorded stable release, else the line's major when a later release on that line is recorded, else the next major. "Newest published stable" is the maximum over the census releases (which trail at 17.4.0), every `retiredAfter` stamp (maximum 17.7.0) and the package label only when the label is stable — under `18.0.0-next.0` the label is excluded, so the answer is 17.7.0, which is right today (npm `latest`); `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` is 18 (`protocol-version.ts:22-25`, lockstep-tested against the package major). Checked by hand: the five 17.7.0 stamps derive 18; 17.5.0 / 17.2.0 / 17.4.0 derive 17; the simulated-facts cases cover a stable 17.x label on the v18 train, the prerelease label, the 18.0.0 label and the 17.x line; once 18.0.0 is the label a 17.7.0 stamp still derives 18. A non-stable stamp throws at module load — loud, not silent.
- Both directions: a joined prescription fails if any named major differs from the derived one (`named.every`), if it names no release at all (`named.length` must exceed 0), or if its `--from` is not `toMajor − 1`. So a 17.7.0-stamped string reverting to 17 fails (the dev's ablations ① ②) and a 17.x-shipped string naming 18 fails (③ ⑤); the construction supports those reported reds, which I did not re-run (read-only).
- Completeness: every retired entry stamped at or above the newest stable must be joined (ablation ④). This is the guard that refuses the merged tree today (`Test Core (1/6)`), which is the pin working as designed.
- Is a guard that makes every future retirement PR edit this pin file an acceptable ratchet? Yes, judged on three points. (1) The failure text is self-explanatory: it names the newest stable release, each offending id with its `retiredAfter`, the map to extend (`JOIN`) and what a row holds ("the tombstones or refusals an author meets for its surface"); vitest prints the file path and line beside it. A dev who has never seen the file can act on it, as the seat's fix round shows. (2) The merge-conflict surface is real but marginal: a retirement PR already edits two shared registries (`conversions/registry.ts` and the ADR-0087 retired-keys entries) and the liveness ledger, so one more shared file changes little; two concurrent retirement PRs that both append to `JOIN` conflict textually at most on adjacent lines, and the resolution is "keep both rows". The repo's stated preference for per-file registration (AGENTS.md on ADR anchors: one file per anchor, no index) names the lower-conflict shape — a per-entry locator on the conversion itself, from which the join is derived with no hand-kept map — but that is a registry type change outside this card, a follow-up and not a defect. (3) The guard refuses only a retirement PR that ships its prescription unjudged, which is the defect this card exists for; it cannot red an unrelated PR. One trap to carry into the fix round: the guard keys on `retiredAfter` being at or above the newest stable, so after `18.0.0` ships, every entry stamped `18.0.0` must be joined too — the ratchet tightens by design, not by accident.
- Should the verdict on `56d63b4e7` be FAIL on this alone? Yes. A PASS record exists to lift the landing, and the landing rule needs every check green; this head's own instrument reds its required test lane on the tree it would land on, and the red is substantive (two prescriptions unjudged), not cosmetic. The diff is not at fault — the same diff on a head that has merged `main` and joined both ids passes this section — but the record is rendered on a head, and this head is not the one to land. The `provider: 'api'` string in ① is a second, independent reason.
- Where it can pass while a string is wrong (named; acceptable for this PR): (1) it compares majors only — "17.6.0" for the sub-day row would pass; the exact 17.5.0 is held by the literal pins in `data/analytics.test.ts` and `driver-memory/src/memory-analytics-time-granularity.test.ts`; (2) rows older than the newest stable are joined only by hand (four are); (3) a retirement with no D2 entry has no `retiredAfter` to derive from — `allowOrgOverride` and `StorageScope.public` as the PR says, every "retired-keys only" row, and now `view.data.provider: 'api'`. `allowOrgOverride`'s "18" is literal-pinned in `metadata-type-registry-allow-org-override-retirement.test.ts`; the StorageScope string has no literal pin on its release (`object-storage.test.ts:59` matches the text without the version). That gap is small — the string is right and the next.0 notes record the removal under `## 18.0.0-next.0` — and the card's nail asks a derived pin only of entries with a `toMajor: 18` registry row, which a D3-only value has none of; a one-line literal pin would close it in the patch round.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `patch`, `Clause-②: no` in both the changeset body and the PR body — RIGHT. No key, value, arm or shape is accepted or refused differently (① above); a wrong release name in shipped prescription text is a bug fix in a released package, which AGENTS.md Post-Task #3 gives a `patch`. Under pre mode this moves the fixed group from `18.0.0-next.0` to `18.0.0-next.1`. No ADR-0087 marker is owed (nothing breaks, nothing registers).

The changeset, sentence by sentence against the head and the published line:
- Line 9: "17.7.0, the newest 17.x release (npm `latest`), still accepts every shape below, and `18.0.0-next.0` is the first release that refuses them." — TRUE: `latest` is 17.7.0 and no 17.8.0 exists; every row is live at the tag tree; every row is refused in the next.0 tarball; nothing was published between them.
- "No 17.x release removes them: the 18 line does." — TRUE.
- The six Was/Now table rows match the diff, including `17.8.0` to 18 and "renamed (no release named)" to "renamed in @objectstack/spec 18".
- "The `18.0.0-next.0` release notes quoted the two `email_template` prescriptions with the earlier version, 17; from this release on they name 18." — TRUE: tarball `CHANGELOG.md:2091` and `:2093` are those two quotes, inside `## 18.0.0-next.0` (header at line 3; `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` on `origin/main` reads the same there). The next release's notes carry this entry, and the stable `18.0.0` aggregate re-renders `22876` with 18 (③ below).
